title: Malacca vs George Town: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: George Town for food and extended stays; Malacca for colonial history and 1–2 day heritage trips. Do both if you have 10+ days in Malaysia.

categories.name: UNESCO Heritage
categories.summary: Both are UNESCO World Heritage sites. Malacca has Portuguese and Dutch colonial layers; George Town has a dense multicultural port city heritage.

categories.name: Food Scene
categories.summary: George Town is a top-5 Southeast Asia food city. Malacca has excellent Nyonya food but narrower scope.

categories.name: Colonial History
categories.summary: Malacca has the deepest colonial layering in Southeast Asia — Portuguese (1511), Dutch (1641), British (1824).

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Malacca is marginally cheaper: RM 80–150/day vs RM 100–180/day in George Town.

categories.name: Time Needed
categories.summary: Malacca is a 1–2 day city. George Town warrants 3–4 days or more.

categories.name: Nightlife
categories.summary: George Town has a year-round bar scene. Malacca depends on the Fri–Sun Jonker Street Night Market.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: George Town unlocks Ipoh, Cameron Highlands, and Langkawi. Malacca mainly offers KL as a day trip.

categories.name: Peranakan Culture
categories.summary: Malacca is the original source of Baba-Nyonya Peranakan culture. The Heritage Museum is outstanding.

faq.question: Is Malacca or George Town better for first-time Malaysia visitors?
faq.answer: George Town is the stronger pick for most first-time visitors. If you have limited time (1–2 days), choose Malacca for a compact heritage experience.

faq.question: How long do you need in each city?
Can you visit both?
faq.answer: Yes — route KL → Malacca (2h south) → KL → Penang (4h north). Allow 12+ days in Malaysia to do both properly.
